
{{alias}}( N, x, strideX , y, strideY)
    Computes the cumulative range of a double-precision floating-point
    strided array.

    The cumulative range at index `i` is defined as

        max(x[0..i]) - min(x[0..i])

    The `N` and stride parameters determine which elements in `x` are accessed
    at runtime and where results are written in `y`.

    Indexing is relative to the first index. To introduce an offset, use a typed
    array view.

    If `N <= 0`, the function returns `y` unchanged.

    Parameters
    ----------
    N: integer
        Number of indexed elements.

    x: Float64Array
        Input array.

    strideX: integer
        Stride length for `x`.

    y: Float64Array
        Output array.

    strideY: integer
        Stride length for `y`.

    Returns
    -------
    out: Float64Array
        Output array.

    Examples
    --------
    // Standard usage:
    > var x = new {{alias:@stdlib/array/float64}}( [ 1.0, -2.0, 2.0 ] );
    > var y = new {{alias:@stdlib/array/float64}}( x.length );
    > {{alias}}( x.length, x, 1, y, 1 )
    <Float64Array>[ 0.0, 3.0, 4.0 ]

    // Using `N` and stride parameters:
    > x = new {{alias:@stdlib/array/float64}}( [ -2.0, 1.0, 1.0, -5.0, 2.0, -1.0 ] );
    > y = new {{alias:@stdlib/array/float64}}( x.length );
    > {{alias}}( 3, x, 2 , y, 1 )
    <Float64Array>[ 0.0, 3.0, 4.0, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0 ]


{{alias}}.ndarray( N, x, strideX, offsetX, y, strideY, offsetY )
    Computes the cumulative range of a double-precision floating-point
    strided array using alternative indexing semantics.

    While typed array views mandate a view offset based on the underlying
    buffer, the `offsetX` parameter supports indexing semantics based on a
    starting index.

    Parameters
    ----------
    N: integer
        Number of indexed elements.

    x: Float64Array
        Input array.

    strideX: integer
        Stride length for `x`.

    offsetX: integer
        Starting index for `x`.

    y: Float64Array
        Output array.

    strideY: integer
        Stride length for `y`.

    offsetY: integer
        Starting index for `y`.

    Returns
    -------
    out: Float64Array
        Cumulative range.

    Examples
    --------
    // Standard usage:
    > var x = new {{alias:@stdlib/array/float64}}( [ 1.0, -2.0, 2.0 ] );
    > var y = new {{alias:@stdlib/array/float64}}( x.length );
    > {{alias}}.ndarray( x.length, x, 1, 0, y, 1, 0 )
    <Float64Array>[ 0.0, 3.0, 4.0 ]

    // Advanced indexing:
    > x = new {{alias:@stdlib/array/float64}}( [ 1.0, -2.0, 3.0, 2.0, 5.0, -1.0 ] );
    > y = new {{alias:@stdlib/array/float64}}( x.length );
    > {{alias}}.ndarray( 3, x, 2, 1 , y, -1, y.length-1 )
    <Float64Array>[ 0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 4.0, 4.0, 0.0 ]

    See Also
    --------
